# Burn

Burns the image away in noisy patches: the paper chars ahead of a glowing edge in the theme accent, and the next image shows through behind it.

<EffectDemo effect="burn" />

## Usage

```ts
import { createTransition, toHoloEffect } from '@mk7s/xtree/core';
import { burn } from '@mk7s/xtree/effects/burn';

const effect = burn({ preset: 'paper' });

// Standalone: blend two textures as progress goes from 0 to 1.
const player = createTransition(renderer, effect, {
  from: textureA,
  to: textureB,
});
player.progress = 0.5;
player.render();

// With HoloCSS: hand it to transition3d().
import { transition3d } from '@mk7s/holocss/three';
await transition3d(fromElement, toElement, toHoloEffect(effect), {
  target,
  update,
});
```

Every parameter is also a property: `effect.scale = 3`. Uniform changes take effect on the next frame without recompiling.

## Parameters

| Parameter   | Type    | Default | Range        | Description                                                                                                                            |
| ----------- | ------- | ------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scale`     | number  | `3`     | 0.5 – 20     | Size of the burning patches: higher values make smaller ones.                                                                          |
| `direction` | number  | `0.3`   | 0 – 1        | How much the burn rises from the bottom instead of spreading in patches.                                                               |
| `edgeWidth` | number  | `0.01`  | 0.002 – 0.05 | Width of the glowing edge, as a fraction of the transition; kept thin so the glow never covers much of the frame at once (WCAG 2.3.1). |
| `glow`      | number  | `3`     | 0 – 10       | Brightness of the edge, in linear units (above 1 blooms).                                                                              |
| `charWidth` | number  | `0.06`  | 0 – 0.3      | Width of the charred margin ahead of the edge.                                                                                         |
| `charring`  | number  | `0.8`   | 0 – 1        | How dark the charred margin gets.                                                                                                      |
| `seed`      | integer | `0`     | 0 – 9999     | Picks the random pattern: the same seed always renders the same frames.                                                                |

Every effect also has `blend` (any of the 26 [blend modes](/reference/shaders#modes)), `opacity` (0–1) and `enabled`.

## Presets

| Preset   | Settings                                     |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `paper`  | `direction: 0`, `scale: 4`, `charWidth: 0.1` |
| `rising` | `direction: 0.8`, `edgeWidth: 0.006`         |
| `embers` | `glow: 6`, `scale: 8`, `charWidth: 0.03`     |
| `clean`  | `charring: 0`, `glow: 1.5`                   |

Apply one with `burn({ preset: 'name' })` or `effect.applyPreset('name')`; presets start from the defaults.

## Details

- **Family:** Transitions · tracked as story X13.7 in the [plan](https://github.com/s4njee/xtree/blob/main/plan.md).
- **Kind:** transition. `createTransition(renderer, effect, { from, to })` runs it on two textures; `toHoloEffect(effect)` turns it into a HoloCSS `ThreeEffect` (parameters are baked in when called), with the `hcss-depth` CSS fallback. See [transitions](/guide/transitions).
- **Motion:** driven by `progress` from your timeline. HoloCSS skips transitions when motion is off; standalone, set `progress = 1` instead of animating.
- **Size:** 7.6 KB gzip budget for `@mk7s/xtree/effects/burn`, including the shared effect runtime.

## Related

- [Crossfade & luma wipe](./crossfade) — Blends to the next image everywhere at once, through noise, or along a luma pattern (linear, radial, diamond or spiral) with a soft edge that can glow in the theme accent.
- [Dissolve](./dissolve) — Burns the surface away as `progress` goes from 0 to 1, in noisy patches or as a front sweeping up the object, with a glowing edge.
- [Wipe](./wipe) — Reveals the next image behind a moving edge: a straight line at any angle, a circle growing from a center, or a clock hand sweeping around it.
